grammar.label: passive with a perfect infinitive — is thought to have been
grammar.form: be + past participle + to have + past participle
grammar.meaning: reports a claim about something already finished

explanation.en: 'The building is thought to have been rebuilt twice' reports a present belief about a past event. The first verb carries the reporting, the second carries the time: 'is thought' now, 'to have been rebuilt' earlier.
explanation.uz: 'The building is thought to have been rebuilt twice' — hozirgi fikr, o'tgan voqea haqida. Birinchi fe'l xabar berishni, ikkinchisi vaqtni bildiradi.

grammar.positive_example: The manuscript is believed to have been copied in the tenth century.
grammar.negative_example: The manuscript is believed to be copied in the tenth century.

l1_notes.uz: Ikki bosqichli zanjir o'zbek tilida bitta qo'shimcha bilan beriladi, shuning uchun 'to have been' tushib qolishi keng tarqalgan.

grammar.label: existential there with a heavy complement
grammar.form: There + be + noun phrase + participle / relative clause / to-infinitive
grammar.meaning: introduces something new when the subject would otherwise be too heavy

explanation.en: English dislikes a long subject: 'There is little evidence to suggest that costs fell' reads better than 'Little evidence to suggest that costs fell exists.' 'There' holds the subject position and the real content follows.
explanation.uz: Ingliz tili uzun egani yoqtirmaydi: 'There is little evidence to suggest…' — 'there' ega o'rnini egallaydi, asosiy mazmun esa keyin keladi.

grammar.positive_example: There remains considerable disagreement about the cause.
grammar.negative_example: Considerable disagreement about the cause remains to exist.

l1_notes.uz: 'There' bu yerda joyni bildirmaydi — u faqat ega o'rnini to'ldiradi.

phonology.label: Rhythm in long noun phrases and nominalised sentences
Vowel reduction in long words — comfortable, vegetable, interesting
Stress shift in word families — PHOtograph, phoTOgrapher, photoGRAPHic

story.title: It is thought to have been

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: This line says the road was built in 1954.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Built by whom? On what evidence?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: None is given. It is thought to have been built by the railway.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Thought by whom? That is the first question the ministry will ask.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: There is a letter in the file that says so, though nobody signed it.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Then write what you can defend, and nothing more.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: 'The road is believed to have been built by the railway. The only source is a letter of 1961 that nobody signed.'

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Longer, and true. A claim without corroboration is not a claim. It is a hope.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: The aforementioned letter is the whole of our evidence.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Then give the extent of it. One letter. Say so.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: There is no verification to be had. Say that too.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: It reads honest. Weak and honest beats strong and purportedly true.
